predeclared_n7_protocol.description: Validation-regime utility comparison: does internal validation regime (A/B/C) predict real external behavior?
predeclared_n7_protocol.inputs: N4's frozen internal per-model pooled MAE (A/B/C) + N6's frozen external per-model MAE (strict cohort, primary; relaxed cohort as a sensitivity cross-check).
primary_analyses: abs_gap(regime, model) = |internal_pooled_MAE(regime, model) - external_MAE(model)|, summarized as the median abs_gap across the 8 models for each regime.
Spearman rank correlation between each regime's model ranking (by internal pooled MAE, ascending) and the external model ranking (by external MAE, ascending).
Kendall tau, same ranking pair, as a second rank-agreement statistic (Spearman and Kendall can disagree on small n=8; both are reported rather than picking whichever looks better).

Top-model selection regret(regime) = external_MAE(argmin_model_by_that_regime) - external_MAE(argmin_model_by_true_external_ranking). Zero regret means the regime's #1 pick was also the truly best external model.

Bootstrap CI (n_boot=2000, seed=20260921, resample external rows with replacement, recompute external MAE per model per resample, then recompute abs_gap/Spearman/Kendall/regret) for the DIFFERENCE between each pair of regimes on each statistic above.
predeclared_n7_protocol.reporting_rule: Report which regime (A, B, or C) best anticipates external behavior on each of the four statistics independently; do not force agreement between statistics, and do not average across statistics into one composite score not specified here.
predeclared_n7_protocol.H1_H2_test: H1 (family-aware validation estimates external error better than random CV): supported if abs_gap(B or C) < abs_gap(A) with the bootstrap CI on that difference excluding zero. H2 (family-aware validation ranks models better): supported if Spearman/Kendall rank agreement with the external ranking is higher for B or C than for A, similarly CI-supported. Both H1 and H2 may be rejected (VALID_NEGATIVE_RESULT) if the CIs include zero or point in the opposite direction -- this is an acceptable, reportable outcome, not a failure to fix.

predeclared_n8_protocol.description: External applicability-domain / risk analysis, computed for ALL 8 models (not only the best by N6, to avoid model-selection-driven cherry-picking of which AD result gets reported).
predeclared_n8_protocol.ad_reference_population: OBELiX development population (449 rows), same as N6's final-fit population -- source-domain AD, not external-cohort-internal AD.
analyses: Spearman(AD_score, |residual|) per model on the strict external cohort.
AD-quartile mean-error table (ad_score_quantile_error_table, n_bins=4) per model.
Risk-coverage curve: pooled MAE at retained coverage 100/75/50/25% (most in-domain rows retained first), per model.
Optional predeclared conformal interval, only if calibrated from OBELiX development data alone; explicitly optional, not required for G4.
predeclared_n8_protocol.h3_test: H3 (AD distance predicts external absolute error and supports useful selective prediction): supported for a given model if Spearman(AD, |error|) > 0 with the correlation's own p-value reported, AND retained-coverage MAE is monotonically non-increasing (allowing at most one non-monotonic step) from 100% to 25% coverage.

G3_validation_regime_comparison_gives_cl.criterion: N7's four primary statistics (median abs_gap, Spearman rank agreement, Kendall tau, selection regret) identify the SAME regime (or the same clearly-worst regime) as most/least externally predictive on at least 2 of the 4 statistics, OR the four statistics consistently show NO regime meaningfully outperforms random CV (a stable, well-documented negative result). G3 FAILS only if the four statistics give mutually contradictory signal with no stable pattern in either direction -- i.e. a genuinely inconclusive result, not merely a negative one.
